 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR HEARING ON I.A, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT Challenging judgment and award dated 06.04.2017 passed by Senior Civil Judge & Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Jewargi (for short, 'tribunal'), in MVC no.552/2012, this appeal is filed.
2.
Shri Basavaraj R. Math, learned counsel for appellant submitted that appeal was by claimant challenging dismissal of claim petition against insurer and seeking enhancement of compensation.

It was submitted that on 09.03.2011, claimant-Smt.Bhima Bai boarded a Commander NC:
2023:KHC-K:7487 Jeep bearing registration no.KA-32/M-6444.
While it was on Chigaralli-Ijeri road, driver of Auto-rickshaw bearing registration no.KA-32/7414, drove it in rash and negligent manner and dashed against claimant causing accident.
In said accident, she sustained multiple fractures of shaft of tibia and fibula etc.
Despite taking treatment, she did not recover fully.
Claiming compensation, she filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act against driver cum owner and insurer of Auto-rickshaw.

sentences.text: Despite service of notice, respondent no.2 did not appear and was placed exparte.
Respondent no.1 did not file objection.
Only insurer filed objection, opposing claim petition on all grounds including violation of permit conditions.

It was specifically contended that at time of accident,
vehicle was plying beyond geographical limit of permit therefore, there was violation of terms and conditions of policy and sought dismissal of claim petition against insurer.
4. Based on pleadings, tribunal framed issued and recorded evidence.
Claimant was examined as PW.1 and Dr.Kishor was examined as PW.2.
Exs. P1
to P15
were marked.

Respondent examined its official as RW.1 and got marked five documents as Exs.R1 to R5.
5.
On consideration, tribunal held that accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Auto-rickshaw by its driver and claimant was entitled for compensation of Rs.3,85,000/-.

However,
on ground that driver of Auto- rickshaw was not having transport endorsement on driving licence and accident had occurred beyond geographical limit of permit, it held insurer not liable to pay compensation and passed award against owner.

6. Assailing said finding, it was submitted that as per Ex.R3-driving licence extract produced by insurer, driver of Auto-rickshaw was holding driving licence to drive light motor vehicle valid from 09.01.2009 to 08.01.2029, which would be valid as on date of accident i.e. 09.03.2011.

In view of decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Mukund Dewangan v/s Oriental Insurance Company Limited,
reported in 2017 (14) SCC 663, same would be sufficient and insurer cannot escape liability.

sentences.text: Insofar as enhancement, it was submitted that claimant was 35 years of age, sustained multiple fractures of shaft of tibia and fibula over right leg assessed by PW.2 to have caused 40% disability to whole body.
However, tribunal considered meager extent of 13% disability which resulted in loss of earning capacity, same would call for interference.
Further it was stated that claimant was earning Rs.12,000/- per month from milk vending etc, tribunal erroneously considered her monthly income at Rs.4,000/-.
Even award under other heads was contended to be inadequate and sought enhancement.
8. On other hand, Sri Sharanabasappa M. Patil, learned counsel for respondent no.3-insurer sought to support impugned award.
It was submitted that there was no dispute about occurrence of accident beyond geographical limit of permit.
Therefore, no interference was warranted.

9. Heard learned counsel and perused impugned judgment and award.
10.

From above submission and since only claimant is in appeal challenging dismissal of claim petition against insurer NC: 2023:KHC-K:7487 and for enhancement of compensation, following points that would arise for consideration are:

sentences.text: "Point no.(i): Whether dismissal of claim petition against insurer was justified?
Point no.(ii): Whether claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation?"

Point no.(i):
11.

From above submission and as observed by tribunal, there is no dispute about driver of Auto-rickshaw holding valid and effective driving licence to drive light motor vehicle from 09.01.2009 to 08.01.2029.
Admittedly insured vehicle was an Auto-rickshaw falling within class of Light Motor Vehicles.
Therefore, as per ratio of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Mukund Dewangan's case (supra), driver would be authorized to drive any light motor vehicle.
Hence, conclusion of tribunal on liability on said aspect would be contrary to law.

12. Though learned counsel for claimant would contend that RW.1 admitted in cross-examination that he did not know distance between accident spot and geographical limit of permit, said contention would be covered by Division Bench decision of this Court in case of Abdul Rouf v/s Megharaj NC: 2023:KHC-K:7487 Mhedole and others (MFA no.201648/2015 C/m, D.D.
26.11.2020), wherein has held that even in said circumstances, insurer could not escape liability insofar as third parties are concerned.

sentences.text: Consequently, point no.(i) would require to be answered in negative.

Point no.(ii):
13.
Though claimant stated that she was 35 years of age and earning Rs.12,000/- per month from milk vending etc, same was not substantiated with specific evidence.
In absence, same has to be assessed notionally.
But, notional income for year 2011 adopted for settlement of cases before Lok Adalath is Rs.6,000/-.
Therefore, same has to be considered.
14. As per medical evidence on record, claimant sustained multiple fractures of shaft of tibia, fibula and chip fracture of condyle of femur.

PW.2 stated that due to above,
claimant had sustained whole body disability of 40%.
Referring to disability certificates issued at Exs.P8 and P9, tribunal has observed that stiffness in ankle and restriction of movement of right leg was noted.
Considering same, assessment of functional disability by tribunal at 13% would be inadequate.
Same has to be considered at 20%.

Thus, compensation towards 'future loss of income' would be:
(Rs.6,000/- x 12 x 16 x 20%) = Rs.2,30,400/-.
15. Tribunal awarded sum of Rs.30,000/- towards pain and suffering.

Considering number of grievous and other non- Smt. Bhima Bai vs Sri. Malappa And Ors on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123486971/
4 grievous fractures sustained by claimant, it would be appropriate to enhance it to Rs.50,000/-.

sentences.text: Normally fractures take about three months to heal.
Considering same as period of lay-off, claimant would be entitled for Rs.18,000/- towards loss of income during laid-up period.

For inpatient period of treatment of 39 days, tribunal awarded Rs.30,000/- towards food, attendant and other incidental charges, which appears to be just and proper, same would not call for interference.
Tribunal awarded Rs.2,05,000/- towards medical expenses against bills produced.
Since same is in complete reimbursement of medical bills produced, same would not call for enhancement.
Tribunal awarded Rs.10,000/- towards loss of amenities which would be inadequate.
It would be appropriate to enhance it to Rs.25,000/-.
Thus, total compensation would be Rs.5,58,400/-.
In view of above, point no.(ii) is answered partly in affirmative.

Consequently, following:
ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) Claimant is held entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,58,400/- as against Rs.3,85,000/- awarded by Tribunal.

Enhanced compensation shall carry interest at 6% from date of petition till deposit.
(iii) Insurer shall deposit entire compensation amount within a period of six weeks from date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
